text: The case screens are served by a gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case and rwb-source-data in parallel, one hop each, and merges the two answers; the route path, merge order and masking rules are left to RWB-PLT-N001-CON
why: Architecture v5 slide 14 and slide 45 fix the parallel-call pattern but not the composite route contract; the app and operations stories need a route to build against
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 notes and slide 45; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-19
confirm: Solution architect confirms the composite route contract
impact: The screens can be built and smoke-tested against the case and source-data operations; the merge and masking detail waits for the platform edge story

text: rwb-case connects with one login of its own, which holds rights in schema rwb_case only and no privilege on another schema; the login name is agreed in the database story of the epic
why: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and DP-02 fix one login per service but no source document gives the name or the grants
read: Template and Rules v1 §R4 and §R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes
confirm: ACE database administrator confirms the login name and grants
impact: No build block: the login is a secret reference and a grant script; the name is filled in when the database story lands

text: The contract baseline fixes the case, account, party and exclusion resource field names, the four case operations, the error envelope, the Idempotency-Key rule and the versioning rule; the field-level required flags and paging parameters are agreed in the baseline review
why: The sources give field names and types but no field-level OpenAPI schema
read: TSD P3 v3 T3.1 and T-A.2; legacy story RWB-E1-018 section 12
confirm: Tech lead and the consuming teams confirm the field-level schema
impact: The app story can build against the named fields and the fakes on Day 1; the field-level detail is a review item, not a build block

text: The rwb-case deployment uses the platform chart with environment values for replicas, resources, zone spread, ingress and probe paths and timings; the values are agreed per environment and never hard-coded in the template
why: The architecture fixes one chart and one pipeline but no document gives the topology detail
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 notes; Template and Rules v1 §R5.5 DP-10 and DP-15
confirm: DevOps engineer and the platform administrator confirm the values per environment
impact: The chart and pipeline can be built and rendered; only the environment values wait for the platform baseline

text: Every document of this legacy key writes 'the rwb-case login (DP-02)' instead of a login name, and the grant scripts take the name from a deployment parameter.
why: Template and Rules §R4 fixes one login per service and DP-02 replaces the shared recovery_svc login, but no source names the rwb-case login.
read: Template and Rules §R4; DP-02; legacy RWB-E1-019 §3 and §13 (shared recovery_svc login).
confirm: ACE DB team, before the wave 1 DB build.
impact: Grants, migrations and runbooks carry a placeholder instead of a name; no business behaviour changes when the name is filled in.

text: Recovery roles, permissions, scope, masking and the delegation-of-authority table are rwb-access (P4) data; rwb-case keeps TEAM as reference data and stores role_code as a code with no foreign key, validated at load time over the rwb-access authorise contract.
why: The ownership map puts role and permission in P4 and the Architecture v5 service contract gives rwb-access the Recovery roles as data; the column-level split is not stated by any source.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 14 and 41; ownership map entries role, permission, masking_rule, delegation_limit; TSD P3 v3 T3.2 LOV-REF-TABLE; DP-01 and DP-08.
confirm: Solution architect with the rwb-access contract owner in RWB-P4-E1037-CON.
impact: The queue load depends on one call to rwb-access per distinct role code; a rwb-access outage refuses the load instead of falling back to a local role copy.

text: The queue_measure columns are taken from TSD P3 v3 T3.1 (DF-RPT-020 to DF-RPT-030) and the list-of-values columns from the reference-data story with DF-REF-028 and DF-REF-029 at minimum; no further column is invented.
why: The legacy story carries no measure column and only two list columns, and both tables are now in the rwb-case schema.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §11; TSD P3 v3 T3.1 queue_measure and LOV-SNAPSHOT-STATUS; FSD P3 v4 FEAT-CWC-18.
confirm: Technical lead, rwb-case, at the first measure publication.
impact: A column needed later is added by a new migration and a new contract version, never by an edit to v1.

text: The Queues template is an xlsx workbook with the sheets QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER, sent as multipart/form-data with file, table and validFrom; the contract accepts it without fixing the column order in v1.
why: The legacy story fixes the request shape and the two sheet names but not the workbook layout.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §4 step 1 and §12 request row; TSD P3 v3 gives no workbook layout.
impact: The app story parses by header name, so a column reorder does not break the load; a new required column needs a checks change.

text: Rollback and verify of reference loads stay with rwb-case as the ownership map records, and are published in a later rwb-case contract story; this legacy key does not claim them in section 12 and tests the two legacy criteria against the contract fake.
why: The ownership map gives both paths owner P3 while the rwb-case operation set stated for this service excludes them.
read: Ownership map entries POST /admin/reference-loads/{loadId}/rollback and .../verify; legacy RWB-E1-019 §12 and AC2, AC7.
confirm: Solution architect at the rwb-case contract review.
impact: A consumer cannot roll back a load through a published operation until the later story lands; the legacy criteria are still owned and tested.

text: RW-TEAMMGR holds Reference data A for the TEAM, QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER tables and approves a queues version, exactly as the legacy story assumes under DL01.
why: The legacy story marks the grant assumed and no BRD, FSD or ownership row confirms it.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-019 §3 bullet 3 and §10; FSD P3 v4 A2.6.3.3.
confirm: Access owner, rwb-access, when the approval grant is loaded as data.
impact: If the grant is wrong, approval is refused with MSG-P4-002 and no version is applied; no data changes.

text: rwb-case connects to ACE PostgreSQL with one per-service login held in Key Vault; the login is named after the schema (rwb_case) until the DBA publishes the final name, and no story hard-codes it.
why: The template requires one login per service and the architecture gives a schema and a login to every service, but no source names it for rwb-case; the three slices of RWB-P3-E1020 still need a credential to deploy, test and call the service.
read: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8 and 41; TSD P3 v3 T2.5
impact: Deployment, connection pool and contract-fake credentials only; no business rule and no business value depends on it.

text: The caseload cap (150 in the legacy examples) stays reference data on queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity, versioned with the QUEUE and QUEUE_MEMBER reference tables; no parameter key is added for it in wave 1.
why: The legacy story reads queue.capacity_cap and queue_member.capacity as facts for the ASSIGNMENT package and cites DL23 for the values; keeping the cap there changes nothing in the data model and keeps the cap versioned with the queue.
read: Legacy RWB-E1-020 sections 8 and 11; TSD P3 v3 T3.1; FSD P3 v4 A2.6
impact: The ASSIGNMENT rule outputs name the cap field only; the source of the value is decided once and applied in the reference-data load.

text: JOB-06 rebalancing runs as its own Temporal Schedule at 06:30 Asia/Bangkok after DailyCaseRun, with overlap policy SKIP and a catch-up window, and its expression is a chart value rather than a constant.
why: The job map gives 06:30 for JOB-06 and names a Schedule, so the time is known even though the relation to the morning run is not written down.
read: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slide 44; FSD P3 v4 A2.17
impact: Ordering of the morning chain only; rebalancing behaviour itself is owned by the E1-030 story.

text: The allocation worker runs as one worker deployment of the rwb-case chart with a horizontal autoscaler bound to the rwb-case task-queue backlog; replica bounds, node pool, connection pool size and the archive of closed run history are chart values with documented defaults, confirmed in SIT.
why: The architecture fixes the api and worker deployment shape and KEDA scaling on backlog but gives no sizing, so the values have to live in the chart and be proven in SIT rather than invented in a story.
read: Arch v5 Text Extract v1 slides 2, 8, 9 and 11; TSD P3 v3 T2.5
impact: Capacity and cost of the service; no business value and no contract shape changes.

text: The per-service login of rwb-case is referred to as "the rwb-case login (DP-02)" until the ACE DB story names it; no document, story, chart or connection string uses the shared monolith login.
why: DP-02 requires one login per service and no source names it; the build, the contract and the chart cannot wait for the name.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R4 (login per service) and section R5.5 DP-02; Architecture v5 slide 41.
impact: A rename touches the vault secret reference and the connection string value only; no code, no schema and no contract change.

text: A transfer refused by the TRANSFER rule, the cap check, the status check or the hold check is final in Epic 1: there is no override path, nothing changes, and the caller may retry with another target owner or queue.
why: No source names a role, endpoint or procedure that may override a refusal, and the legacy contract has no error that an override would answer.
read: RWB-E1-021 exception paths X2, X3, X4, X9, X10; FSD P3 v4 A2.10 VR-P3-010-1 and VR-P3-010-2; no override rule in the Business Rules and Routing Logic extract.
impact: If an override is confirmed, one acceptance criterion, one authority row and one runbook section are added to the Epic 2 transfer screen story; no schema change.

text: The transfer reason list is reference data of rwb-case: P3 owns the LOV-TRANSFER-REASON rows, the business owner of DL23 approves additions and retirements through the reference-load approve operation, and the published contract references the list without enumerating it.
why: The R-PREC default ruling gives reference data to P3 and DP-07 gives rwb-case the reference-data contract, but no source names the owner of this one list.
read: Template and Rules v1 section R3 default rulings and section R5.5 DP-07; TSD P3 v3 T3.2; RWB-E1-021 sections 3 and 13.
impact: None on the schema or the contract shape; a list change is a dated reference-data load with an approver, and a client that hard-coded the codes would need its enum refreshed.

text: The chart ships no environment default for cluster, node pool, replica counts, ingress host, resource limits or the pod disruption budget; every one is a value supplied by the platform team, and the two-replica starting values for the api and the worker are proposals to be confirmed at the wave-1 release rehearsal.
why: No source specifies the deployment topology of any service, and a hard-coded default would become an undocumented production decision.
read: Architecture v5 slides 4 and 20 (api and worker deployment per service); Template and Rules v1 section R4.
impact: Values only; no code, schema or contract change. A sizing decision changes the values file per environment.

text: Every reference to the rwb-case database login names it as the rwb-case login (DP-02) and its literal name is taken from RWB-PLT-DB when issued; the grants are SELECT, INSERT and UPDATE on schema rwb_case only and nothing on another schema.
why: Template and Rules R4 requires one login per service and DP-02 retires recovery_svc, but no source gives the name, so the story cannot be written without a decision.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41 and slide 9 note; Template and Rules v1 R4 and R5.5 DP-02; TSD P3 v3 T6.2
applied_in: RWB P3 E1023 APP Case record view v1, read only v1.md sections 3, 10 and 13; RWB P3 E1023 CON Case record view v1, read only - contract v1.md section 3
impact: The Flyway grant script, the connection pool configuration and the deployment manifest carry a placeholder until the login is issued; no code change is needed when it lands.

text: SCR-03 is served by one gateway-bff composite route that calls rwb-case GET /cases/{caseId} and, in parallel, rwb-source-data for the customer and account parts, merges the answers into one screen model, and fails one section at a time with MSG-P3-023 when a call fails.
why: The screen is a composite at the edge and neither the route nor the merge rule is specified, so the story and the contract need a read shape and a failure rule to test against.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 10 walkthrough note and slide 21 composite route note; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-19
applied_in: RWB P3 E1023 APP Case record view v1, read only v1.md sections 3, 5, 13 and 15; RWB P3 E1023 CON Case record view v1, read only - contract v1.md sections 3, 7 and 12.8
impact: The screen model and the section-level degradation can be built and tested against the stub; a different merge in RWB-PLT-N001-CON changes the stub only.

text: The masking contract is keyed by view field ID and returns, per field, a masked flag and the source column to read; rwb-case sends the field list it read and applies the answer with the guard library, and the access record carries the same field IDs and masked flags.
why: The masking hook of every personal field must be published in the contract and tested with a fake, and the payload shape is absent from every source.
read: RWB-P4-E1039-CON contract line; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 14 rwb-access contract; DP-08; DL26
applied_in: RWB P3 E1023 APP Case record view v1, read only v1.md sections 3, 8 and 13; RWB P3 E1023 CON Case record view v1, read only - contract v1.md sections 7, 11 and 12.8
impact: The personal fields stay marked with the field ID of the data dictionary; a different payload changes the client adapter and the fake only.

text: The timeline is read with page and size parameters, ordered by occurred_at descending with the source system on each row, and the ledger rows come from an interaction read operation of the rwb-source-data contract that carries the same paging; the page size value is a parameter, not a constant in code.
why: The timeline cannot be composed or tested without a read operation and a paging rule, and the legacy paging values are not carried into the P1 contract.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 15 rwb-source-data contract; DP-18; TSD P3 v3 API-P3-003; legacy RWB-E1-023 section 12
applied_in: RWB P3 E1023 APP Case record view v1, read only v1.md sections 8 and 12.2; RWB P3 E1023 CON Case record view v1, read only - contract v1.md sections 11, 12.1 and 12.2
impact: The timeline and the contact history can be built and tested against the fake with a default page size; the value moves to a parameter when the P1 contract publishes it.
